text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, such as GET or POST, to a specific endpoint. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before using an API, you usually need authentication, often through an API key, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, always include error handling in your code, because requests can fail for many reasons, such as network problems or invalid input.
